verdictReason: Killed on three major reasons: (1) paid homeowner traffic (~$149/lead non-branded, 25-40% booking) costs far more per booked job than the $100 fee, triggering the scan-1 falsifier; (2) the only cheaper route is SEO/rank-and-rent, 3-6 months and copyable, so no exclusive/compounding edge and no day-45 revenue; (3) pay-on-contact Thumbtack, exclusive-lead vendors, Takl and Google LSA already cover the wedge. Pessimistic year-1 model loses ~$1.9k.

answers.question: (1) What free/cheap alternative covers the wedge?
answers.answer: Several partly do. Thumbtack is free to join and bills when a customer contacts or hires the pro, with a weekly budget cap (D1, D2, D3). Google LSA bills only valid leads at roughly $18-$45 per house-cleaning lead and $15-$30 per handyman lead per agency blogs (D6, D17; D16 says cleaners spend $60-70). Takl already charges only on completed jobs, 10%-30% (D4). Exclusive leads are sold by vendors at 2-3x shared price (D10, D11). Cleaning/handyman lead prices are already low (D9), so the per-booking saving vs a $100 fee is small or zero. The scan-1 ~$350 per booked job incumbent figure came from a blog (E4) that I could not re-read (fetch refused), so it stays unverified.

answers.question: (2) What structural edge exists, and who could copy it?
answers.answer: None identified. Single-pro routing and pay-on-outcome pricing are product choices that Thumbtack, Takl, lead vendors or any rank-and-rent operator could copy (D4, D10, D11). The only possible compounding asset is a locally ranked site, but ranking takes 3-6 months, is not exclusive, and Google Business Profile access is restricted to genuine service providers (D12, D14). Falsifier: evidence that a zero-audience entrant can rank for "trade + metro" within ~4 months at <$1,500 and that pros will pay a per-booking fee to an unknown intermediary; no such evidence found.

answers.question: (3) Who demonstrably pays and how much?
answers.answer: Pros demonstrably pay per lead: Thumbtack $10-$100+ per lead by pro self-report (D5; scan-1 E1 $15-$80), Google LSA $15-$45 for cleaning/handyman (D6, D17) and ~$53-$149 per lead in Google Search/LSA for home services overall (D8). Nothing found shows pros paying a pay-on-booking fee to a new intermediary; the only analogue is Takl taking 10%-30% of completed jobs (D4).

answers.question: (4) Legal/platform constraints?
answers.answer: Google Business Profile limits listings to genuine, staffed service businesses and bars virtual offices (D14); LSA verifies the advertiser's licence, insurance and background (D15), so a non-provider entrant likely cannot use either channel in its own name (not confirmed). Lead-gen carries TCPA exposure of $500-$1,500 per call/text per one vendor blog (not independently confirmed). State contractor-licence rules for handyman work, and whether a percentage-of-job referral fee is allowed in a given state, could not be verified (state licensing pages refused/errored); restrict to licence-free house cleaning and have counsel review.

answers.question: (5) Year-1 numbers (reference entrant: $3,500, 17 h/week)?
answers.answer: Model for house cleaning in one metro, SEO-led, $100 fee per booked job (assumption). Base: no revenue months 1-3 (D12), requests ramp 5 to 45/month over months 4-12 = 225 requests (assumption), 40% book (upper end of D7), 70% of fees actually collected (assumption: 30% off-platform leakage), giving revenue ~$6,300; cost ~$2,980 (site $300, content/links $1,200, tools $480, legal $700, tests $300, all assumptions); profit ~+$3,300. Pessimistic (price x0.8, volume x0.5, cost x1.5): revenue ~$2,520, cost ~$4,470, profit ~-$1,950. Paid-traffic variant: $149/lead (D8) at 40% booking = ~$372 per booked job vs $100 fee, a loss on every job; even at LSA-level $18-$45/lead and 25-40% booking, cost is $45-$180 per booked job, with no margin at the high end. The base case rests on an unsourced demand ramp; the pessimistic case fails.

newEvidence.quote: You pay when a new customer contacts or hires you.
newEvidence.shows: Thumbtack itself now bills the pro when a customer contacts or hires them (customer-initiated), which weakens the scan-1 pain that pros are billed whether or not the homeowner replies.

newEvidence.quote: Creating an account is free. There's no signup or subscription fee.
newEvidence.shows: Answers the scan-1 unknown "does Thumbtack have a free tier": free to join, pay per contact, weekly budget set by the pro.

newEvidence.quote: You will be charged for a lead the moment the customer reaches out.
newEvidence.shows: A Thumbtack administrator states the charge trigger is the customer reaching out to the pro, i.e. the lead is not billed on a pro-initiated message to a silent homeowner.

newEvidence.quote: Takl will take a 10%-30% cut from each job you complete
newEvidence.shows: An existing marketplace (Takl) already charges the pro only on completed jobs (10%-30% cut, plus $2.99/month access fee per the same page), i.e. the pay-on-outcome wedge is not new. Publisher is a Thumbtack competitor, so treat as secondary.

newEvidence.quote: If a lead doesn't turn into a job, you don't get your money back.
newEvidence.shows: Pro complaint about non-refunded leads on Thumbtack persists (pain is real), but figures are pro self-reports from a competitor-published page.

newEvidence.publisher: Plyrium Academy: Google LSA cost article (agency blog)
newEvidence.shows: Google Local Services Ads average cost per lead for house cleaning is $18-$45 (agency blog, secondary). A cheap per-lead alternative to the entrant for cleaning pros that qualify for LSA.

newEvidence.publisher: Plyrium Academy: Google LSA cost article (agency blog)
newEvidence.shows: Booking share of qualified leads is 25-40%, used to convert cost per lead into cost per booked job.

newEvidence.quote: The SearchLight breakdown put branded search at a $34 cost per lead, non-branded search at $149, and Performance Max at $72,

newEvidence.shows: Home-services Google Search Ads cost ~$149 per lead on non-branded terms (the terms a new lead-gen site must buy). Same page: blended $104 per lead; LSA ~ $53. Secondary source quoting a third-party dataset.

newEvidence.quote: typically see the lowest lead costs, ranging from $15 to $50,
newEvidence.publisher: ClicksGeek: Pay per lead services pricing (vendor blog)
newEvidence.shows: Local-service/cleaning lead costs are the lowest of the trades at $15-$50 per lead (vendor blog; not trade-specific): a low per-lead price anchor that the entrant must beat per booking.

newEvidence.quote: often two to three times the price of shared leads,
newEvidence.publisher: ClicksGeek: Pay per lead services pricing (vendor blog)
newEvidence.shows: Exclusive leads are an established product that command 2-3x the shared price; exclusivity is therefore already sold by existing lead vendors and priced into the market.

newEvidence.publisher: Prospeo: Lead gen business model explained (vendor blog)
newEvidence.shows: Rank-and-rent depends on SEO and needs 3-6 months before consistent ranking, so first revenue at day 45 (reference entrant) is not credible from SEO alone.

newEvidence.quote: you'll spend half your time arguing about refunds.
newEvidence.publisher: Prospeo: Lead gen business model explained (vendor blog)
newEvidence.shows: Lead-quality disputes with buyers are a known operating cost of lead-gen without written acceptance criteria.

newEvidence.shows: Google Business Profile (the map-pack channel that drives local home-service leads) is restricted to businesses that really operate at/serve from the address; a non-provider lead-gen entrant cannot plainly hold such a listing for the trade. Page does not ban lead-gen outright (it addresses individual practitioners and virtual offices).

newEvidence.shows: LSA verification (licence/registration, insurance, background checks) applies to the advertiser itself; whether a non-provider lead-gen entrant could buy LSA is not established, so the cheap LSA lead price ($18-$45 cleaning) may not be available to the entrant (unverified).

newEvidence.shows: Pay-on-contact already exists on Google LSA for cleaners; same page says cleaning companies spend around $60-70 per lead, so sources disagree with D6 ($18-$45).

newEvidence.publisher: Adapt Digital Solutions: Google LSA for contractors (agency blog)
newEvidence.shows: Handyman is the low-ticket trade the idea targets, and its Google LSA per-lead cost is only $15-$30, so pro lead cost is already small relative to a $100 per-booking fee.

newAlternatives.label: Thumbtack pro account: free to join, pay when a customer contacts/hires, weekly budget cap (cost varies; $0 fixed)
Google Local Services Ads (pay per valid lead; house cleaning $18-$45/lead, handyman $15-$30/lead per agency blogs)
Takl: $2.99/month access fee plus 10%-30% cut of completed jobs (pay-on-outcome marketplace)
Vendor-sold exclusive home-services leads (priced 2-3x shared leads; no per-booking terms found)
Rank-and-rent / own local site (pro builds own SEO presence; rank-and-rent sites quoted at $1,000-$2,000/month by a vendor blog)

killReasons.reason: Paid homeowner traffic costs more per booked job than the $100 fee the entrant would charge: non-branded home-services Google Search Ads run ~$149 per lead (D8) and only 25-40% of qualified leads book (D7), i.e. roughly $370-$600 per booked job before the entrant takes any margin; break-even fee on this route is >$500. The scan-1 falsifier (traffic cost per booked job above ~$100) is triggered on the paid route.

The only route that could undercut paid traffic is organic SEO / rank-and-rent, which needs 3-6 months to rank (D12), so the reference entrant's 45-day first revenue does not hold, and rankings are not an exclusive or compounding asset a rival could not copy (anyone can build a competing site; Google Business Profile access is limited to real providers, D14). No structural edge survives.

Each element of the wedge is already available: Thumbtack is free to join with a weekly budget and bills when a customer contacts or hires the pro (D1, D2, D3); exclusive leads are sold by lead vendors at 2-3x shared price (D10, D11); Takl already takes a cut only on completed jobs (D4); Google LSA bills only valid leads at $15-$45 for handyman/cleaning (D6, D17). The scan-1 premise that pros pay whether or not homeowners reply is partly stale (D1, D3).

Pay-on-confirmed-booking cannot be verified unless homeowner payment runs through the entrant; no source shows pros accept a fee from an unknown intermediary, and quality disputes consume time (D13). Off-platform leakage rate could not be sourced.

assumptions: Trade: house cleaning (licence-free in most places; not verified), one metro; fee $100 per confirmed booked job (scan-1 assumption, not an observed price).
No revenue months 1-3 because SEO needs 3-6 months (D12); monthly homeowner requests ramp 5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45 over months 4-12 = 225 (assumption, unsourced).
Booking rate 40% of requests routed to the single pro (top of 25-40% range, D7); fee collection rate 70% (assumption: 30% off-platform leakage).
Cost: domain/site $300, content/links/citations $1,200, call/SMS/CRM/payment tools $40/month, legal/LLC/terms $700, tests $300 = $2,980 (all assumptions); owner time unpaid (17 h/week).
Pessimistic: price x0.8 ($80), volume x0.5 (112 requests), cost x1.5 ($4,470) gives revenue $2,520 and profit -$1,950.
Paid variant: Google non-branded $149/lead (D8) / 40% booking = $372 per booked job; break-even fee about $532 after 30% leakage.

legalNotes: Google Business Profile guidelines restrict listings to businesses that operate at or serve from the address and bar unstaffed virtual offices (D14).
Google LSA screens the advertiser (licence/registration, insurance, background) (D15); a lead-gen entrant that is not itself the provider may not be eligible (unconfirmed).
TCPA penalties of $500-$1,500 per unconsented call/text are cited by a vendor blog (D13 page); homeowner consent capture needed if the entrant routes calls/texts (not independently confirmed).
State contractor-licence thresholds for handyman work and rules on referral/percentage fees to licensed contractors not verified; restrict to licence-free trades and obtain counsel review.
Holding homeowner payments (to verify bookings) may trigger money-transmission rules; use a licensed processor/escrow rather than holding funds (not researched).
